Careful habits for greeting routines in detail
Everyone on the desk should know why careful work counts

Companion Animal Travel Desk Greeting and Intake Practices
This section explains how the Companion Animal Travel Desk welcomes travelers with companion animals and records each visit with steady care.

Staff should greet each traveler in a calm, respectful way and make space for pets to settle before any questions begin. Clear, friendly language helps reduce stress and keeps the desk experience smooth for everyone. The desk ledger must reflect any service changes, special handling notes, or travel concerns as soon as they are confirmed, because accurate records protect the animal and support the rest of the journey.

The safety coordinator reviews hazards and prevention steps with the team and should be included whenever a pet shows signs of distress, travel discomfort, or unusual behavior. If a crate, leash, carrier, or document appears out of order, staff should pause the intake flow and resolve the issue before moving ahead. Clean surfaces, tidy waiting areas, and gentle handling are part of normal service, not extra effort. Staff should also keep communication prompt and respectful when speaking with the traveler, the carrier team, and other desk colleagues. <<FACT F025>> Careful review of kennel use, lounge access, and routing notes helps the desk avoid confusion and keeps animals moving through the process with less strain. <<FACT F004>> When a concern cannot be settled at the counter, the matter should go to the safety coordinator or the senior coordinator right away.

For questions about this section, contact the safety coordinator or the senior coordinator at Aurelia Skyways.
